case.question: I fish from the pier for salmon. For this week, how good do you expect pier fishing for salmon to be at each of St. Joseph, South Haven, Grand Haven and Muskegon? Rate each port 0-4 (0 slow, 1 below average, 2 average, 3 good, 4 excellent) and say which you'd go to.

events.text:
## Recommendation

- **Go to the Grand Haven pier.** It's the only pier report this spring with a non-spawn lure working.
- **Expect slow fishing, roughly 1 out of 4.** Plan on a few coho, not a bite.
- **Try orange spoons or alewife first.** Spawn on the bottom also caught coho at St. Joseph and South Haven.
- **Don't count on Muskegon's pier.** No pier report exists there this spring, so I can't rate it.

## Why

- Grand Haven's most recent pier report (May 18) is the only one where anglers caught coho on alewives or orange spoons (Grand Haven, 2022-05-18).
- The May 18 St. Joseph and South Haven pier reports were both rated 1 (below average), with only occasional coho on spawn (St. Joseph, 2022-05-18; South Haven, 2022-05-18).
- Boats did better than the pier at Muskegon and Grand Haven, rated 3 (good), so if the pier stays slow, a boat is the bigger bet (Muskegon, 2022-05-18; Grand Haven, 2022-05-18).

## Evidence

**Recent reports (newest is May 18, six days old)**
- Grand Haven pier: "Pier anglers were catching a few coho salmon on alewives or while casting orange spoons." Quality 1 (Grand Haven, 2022-05-18).
- South Haven pier: "Pier fishing remained slow but there was an occasional coho caught on spawn." Quality 1 (South Haven, 2022-05-18).
- St. Joseph pier: "Anglers were also catching an occasional coho. … Nightcrawlers were catching the catfish while spawn was catching the coho." Quality 1 (St. Joseph, 2022-05-18).
- Muskegon: the May 18 report covers boats only. Boats were rated 3, with fish 35 to 90 feet down (Muskegon, 2022-05-18).
- Earlier pier reports were all rated 0 or 1 (for example, Grand Haven, 2022-04-27: "slow"). None of them show a pier rating above 1.

**Past seasons**
- The similar-water search (surface about 53 F, within 21 days of today) returned only this spring's reports. It found no earlier seasons, so I have no history for what usually follows.

**Conditions now**
- The conditions tool was in backtest mode. Live data was unavailable, so these figures are for the week before May 24, not today.
- Buoy surface water (45168, serving St. Joseph and South Haven) averaged 53 F and fell 4 F over that week. Buoy 45029 (Grand Haven and Muskegon) averaged 52 F, down 3 F (Conditions, week before 2022-05-24).
- No modeled pierhead water or wind forecast was available. I can't check for an upwelling at the piers.

## Caveats

- The newest report is six days old, and the season can change fast. Treat this as a guide and check the next DNR bulletin.
- The 53 F and 52 F figures are buoy readings from miles offshore, not pier water temperature.
- Muskegon's pier has no report this spring, so its "no rating" is a gap, not a sign of poor fishing.
- Ratings reflect the DNR's wording. Pier results have been consistently slow this spring, so expect little action.

## Sources

- DNR bulletin, week of May 18: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3186585
- DNR bulletin, week of May 4: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3166173
- DNR bulletin, week of April 27: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3155afc
